thread:
alex: Quick FYI — seeing a regression in KV-eviction tail latency on the nightly perf run. Looks like a kernel selection shift around long sequences. I'm going to capture with nsys but want tips on flags (osrt/nvtx/cuda) and sampling window.
priya: I had similar. Use NVTX ranges to bracket the request path, then capture only that range with `--capture-range=nvtx`. Keeps traces small.
jon: Command I use:
```
nsys profile --output=kv-evict-trace --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=0 --capture-range-end=0 --sampling=cpu --sample-interval=1000000 --duration=30s
```
(priya: note some flags differ by nsys versions — check `nsys --help`)
emma: Also try two runs: short burst (2-5s) with high fidelity, and a long run (30-60s) with sampling enabled. Sampling bias can hide microsecond spikes if window too short.
alex: Good point. What's a reasonable sample interval? I want to catch 20–200us kernels.
priya: For that range you'll need lower sample interval — e.g., `--sample-interval=100000` (100us) but file size will blow up. Alternative: use osrt + continuous tracing for kernel timelines and then sample cpu stacks for hotspots.
jon: TL;DR: Use `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` + NVTX bracketing for focused captures, `--capture-range=process:<pid>` if you can't instrument NVTX, and `--sample-interval` tuned to expected kernel duration.
perf-bot: scheduled perf job kv-evict-nightly started: https://perf.internal/runs/kv-evict/214 — I'll post the nsys link when done :robot_face: 
emma: Also check kv cache behavior — sometimes eviction causes many small kernels; batching heuristics may force different kernels (FP32->FP16 path) which changes kernel IDs. Use `--force-overwrite` on output to iterate quickly.
alex: Sharing quick NVTX snippet I'm inserting:
```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("request_start");
// run inference
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
jon: If you want chronological kernel timeline, enable `--trace=osrt` — OSRT shows CPU-side scheduling and helps correlate batching decisions to kernel launches.
priya: If trace gets too big, compress with `nsys export` or filter with `nsys stats` to get hot kernels only. Also keep seed inputs stable — batching distribution matters a lot.
emma: One more gotcha: when using dedicated GPUs with MIG or MPS, kernel scheduling differs — include hardware tags in trace notes.
alex: Thanks — I'll run a short NVTX-bracketed capture with 200us sample-interval and post the link.
